column12: We disapprove any contrary statement in Redondo-Lemos.
To the extent Hays v. Arave, 977 F.2d 475 (9lh Cir.1992), on which the panel relied in reaching the opposite conclusion, is inconsistent with our analysis, it is hereby overruled.
To the extent Mitchell is inconsistent with this opinion, we overrule it.
In conclusion, we overrule Pettaway.
We therefore overrule Arreola v. Mangaong, 65 F.3d 801.
To the extent that our decision in United States v. Albertini, 830 F.2d 985 (9th Cir.1987), conflicts with Rodgers, we overrule Albertini.
To the extent that our case law holds to the contrary, it is overruled.
To the extent that Nordby is inconsistent with this opinion, it is overruled.
To the extent that Sugiyama and Perez address the transport of drugs through international airspace on a nonstop domestic flight, they are overruled.
For all of the foregoing reasons, we overrule our decision in Duffield.
To the extent that any of our prior case law, including Willhoite, suggests otherwise, those cases are overruled.
Any statement to the contrary in McMullen v. INS, 788 F.2d 591, 598 (9th Cir.1986), is overruled.
Therefore, we overrule Williams, clarify Hernandez-Hernandez, vacate Gonzales’s sentence and remand for resentencing.
To the extent Morton suggests or is interpreted to the contrary, it is overruled.
United States v. Diaz-Argueta, 447 F.3d 1167, 1169 (9th Cir.2006), which suggested the contrary, is to that extent overruled.
We thus overrule Tapia-Acuna’s holding that there’s no rational basis for providing section 212(c) relief from inadmissibility, but not deportation.
To the extent Ladha v. INS, 215 F.3d 889, 903 (9th Cir.2000), is to the contrary, it is overruled.

To the extent Molski required the district court to inquire only into the intent of the plaintiffs and focus primarily on determining whether reasonable plaintiffs would bring suit to obtain injunctive or declaratory relief even in the absence of a possible monetary recovery, see Molski, 318 F.3d at 950 & n. 15, it is overruled.
In the course of doing so, sitting as an en banc court, we overrule our equal protection holding in Lujan-Armendariz v. INS, 222 F.3d 728 (9th Cir.2000).
We therefore overrule Rice v. Holder, 597 F.3d 952 (9th Cir.2010).

We overrule that portion of Navarro-Lopez.
We overrule Sandoval-Lua, v. Gonzales, 499 F.3d 1121, 1130-31 (9th Cir.2007), and Rosas-Castaneda v. Holder, 655 F.3d 875, 883-84 (9th Cir. 2011), to the extent that they conflict with this holding.
